items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: I played from two in the afternoon ‘til eight at night with the older guys, and then at ten to four AM with Henry “Red” Allen at night.

ctx.x: I just wondered if you were like pinching yourself.
I was playing both shifts, man. I played from two in the afternoon ‘til eight at night with the older guys, and then at ten to four AM with Henry “Red” Allen at night. And so, there

used to be a place across the street called the Copper Rail. It was a soul food place. And all those old guys from the old school jazz, they were all drinkers. “Have a drink, have a drink.” By the time it was 8:00 I was out of it. And the bar tender would be sending me up pieces of Italian bread to soak up, so I could play the gig. But I was learning a lot. And then I got to — I went to Chicago with Jimmy McPartland. And I met this boxer, Connie Milano. And he said he was a friend of Oscar Peterson’s and that…
